question.prompt:
When the mean, median, and mode of the list \[10, 2, 5, 2, 4, 2, x\]

are arranged in increasing order, they form a non-constant arithmetic progression. What is the sum of all possible real values of \(x?\)

solutions.explanation:
The mode is always \(2\): it occurs at least three times, while every other value occurs at most twice. The mean is
\[
\mu=\frac{25+x}{7}.
\]
To find the median, insert \(x\) into the sorted fixed entries \(2,2,2,4,5,10\) and take the fourth entry. This gives three exhaustive cases.

If \(x\le2\), the median is \(2\), equal to the mode. A nonconstant arithmetic progression of three numbers has three distinct terms, so this case gives no solutions.

If \(2<x<4\), the median is \(x\). Also
\[
\mu-x=\frac{25-6x}{7}>0,
\]
so the statistics in increasing order are \(2,x,\mu\). Equal consecutive differences require the middle term to be the average of the endpoints:
\[
2x=2+\frac{25+x}{7}.
\]
Multiplying by \(7\) gives \(14x=39+x\), so \(x=3\). This lies in the required interval and gives \((2,3,4)\).

If \(x\ge4\), the median is \(4\), and \(\mu\ge29/7>4\). Thus the increasing order is \(2,4,\mu\), and
\[
2\cdot4=2+\frac{25+x}{7}.
\]
This gives \(25+x=42\), so \(x=17\). It satisfies \(x\ge4\) and gives \((2,4,6)\).

These cases include both boundary values \(2\) and \(4\), so all possibilities have been covered. The requested sum is \(3+17=\boxed{20}\), choice E.
solutions.title: Separate the possible median positions
